product.schneider-euroat.summary: The compact AT in the Euro range combines a separate keyboard, AT-Bus disk and integrated EGA video.
product.schneider-euroat.history: EuroAT brought Schneider's compact range into the AT class alongside the PC/XT-class EuroPC and EuroXT. Old Crap classifies it under 1989, although its page does not establish when sales began. Happy Computer presented it as new in February 1990: 2,998 DM with a monochrome monitor and 40 MB hard disk, in a comparison of affordable ATs. It offered an alternative for DOS applications with more memory and storage. Schneider's manual identifies a EuroAT-specific board; the preserved sources do not reliably establish an external OEM manufacturer or the first sale date.
product.schneider-euroat.technical.confi: The review separates the exact price from a rounded figure. The text gives 2,998 DM and the table 3,000 DM; Works with a mouse added 250 DM. The tested configuration had 1 MB and a 3.5-inch 1.44 MB floppy drive.
product.schneider-euroat.technical.board: Its electronics differ from PC2640's. The manual identifies GC101A, two GC102A chips, JIM TC110G008, a Dallas DS1287 RTC and an 8042 keyboard controller; the parts list and review agree on 12 MHz.
product.schneider-euroat.technical.memor: Standard memory was 1 MB. Happy Computer says it could not be expanded on the board; its table documents two free slots. This limitation must not be confused with the total capacity attainable through cards.
product.schneider-euroat.technical.video: Integrated video supported more than the supplied monitor. The review describes 640 × 350 EGA and up to 800 × 600 with a multisync monitor. The manual lists GC201 logic; the preserved EuroVGA ROM belongs to a variant requiring board-level confirmation.
product.schneider-euroat.technical.firmw: Firmware is preserved for researching variants. BIOS 2.01A and 2.03 each comprise two 32 KiB chips, alongside 64 KiB EuroVGA 1.02. Hashes have been checked; this is neither a complete EGA set nor a boot test.
product.schneider-euroat.technical.verif: Preservation has verified files, not operation. No dedicated EuroAT entry was found in BluMach 2fb7451a; MAME marks the model as not working in the preserved source.
product.schneider-euroat.technical.limit: Each BIOS still needs to be matched to its board and video. Booting, memory, keyboard, RTC and AT-Bus disk are unvalidated in BluMach. A publishable photograph and creation profile remain pending.
product.schneider-euroat.technical.manua: Schneider, Service Manual Euro AT, Ident-Nr. 43490: component list, printed page 44; original preserved. The Old Crap page, published on 28 April 2024, classifies the machine under 1989.
product.schneider-euroat.technical.prima: Happy Computer 02/1990, AT comparison, pp. 32–33, Alfred Poschmann: EuroAT price, equipment, memory, video and testing; scan preserved.
product.schneider-euroat.technical.secon: MAME, at.cpp: euroat 2.01/2.03 sets, EuroVGA 1.02 and not-working status; this does not prove universal compatibility between variants.
product.schneider-euroat.warning: Historical sheet under research; booting in BluMach has not been validated.
product.schneider-euroat.technical.code: BluMach 2fb7451a, machine table: preserved code inspection; no dedicated entry for this model was found.
